assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED opened a genuinely new regime: strong, controllable coupling of a single artificial atom to a single microwave photon on a chip. It is the architecture behind dispersive readout, quantum-nondemolition measurement, two-qubit gates and bus-mediated coupling, and it unified waveguide and microwave quantum optics with qubit control. The discovery, not merely the application, is clean and has changed how a whole field works.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huard, Girvin and Schoelkopf's 2004 proposal and the Wallraff et al. 2004 Nature demonstration are the core. Of the three credited names, Blais (theory), Wallraff (first strong-coupling experiment and later circuit-QED developments) and Schoelkopf (Yale group, transmon and cQED architecture) give a sensible trio. Allocation is not fully clean because Girvin, Devoret and others in the Yale circle are not in the credited list, and the 2025 prize already recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended in dozens of laboratories over two decades, including our own at Chalmers, with stable interpretation. Timing is good, and recognition now would complement the 2025 prize rather than duplicate it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) may make the committee judge the area recently rewarded.
Credit among the Yale theory and experiment group, and the omission of Girvin, is unresolved by the supplied names.
I work in this field and my judgement may be biased by proximity; I acknowledge that and defer on credit to colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller 1995 proposal for quantum logic with trapped ions, and its experimental realisation with high-fidelity gates and entanglement of many ions, defined the first physically complete platform for quantum computation. It is original, conceptually crisp and has had very large influence on quantum information experiments.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators. Blatt is a defensible experimental representative among several, but Wineland (already a 2012 laureate), Monroe, Wineland's NIST group and others also made decisive contributions, so the experimental slot is contestable. A two-person theory prize is possible.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: ion-trap gates, entanglement of tens of ions and error-correction demonstrations are reproduced across many groups. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems may limit novelty in the committee's view.
Whether Blatt or another experimentalist best completes the trio is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based Ekert protocol founded quantum cryptography and the idea that quantum physics provides information-theoretic security. It is a deep, original idea that became a field, with real experimental implementations.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard for BB84 and Ekert for E91 are a natural and fair trio, with little credit ambiguity; Bennett and Brassard were also part of teleportation work already recognised in 2022 via Zeilinger.
assessment.maturity: Satellite and fibre experiments over many years confirm feasibility, though practical security against device imperfections is still developing. Physics content is mature; the commercial maturity is not what the prize rewards.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as physics or computer science and cryptography.
B056 is a near-duplicate entry with teleportation added; I rank this one to avoid the part overlapping the 2022 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, via Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and many-body effects, brought clocks to the 10^-18 level and opened tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. Clear invention, clear physics and strong lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye drove the precision, so two laureates is clean. Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland's ion clocks (2012) are already recognised, but this credit is distinct. Others such as Lemonde, Takamoto or Ludlow are omitted.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide, with redefinition of the SI second under discussion. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes in precision metrology.
Allocation to a possible third contributor is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, single-site microscopy and Hubbard-model studies) made controllable many-body quantum systems available. It is a clear new capability for studying fundamental phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch for theory, Greiner and Bloch for experiments (Mott transition with Hänsch's group), is a plausible split. Jaksch is not in the credited names, and Bloch credit overlaps with B048 and B035 entries, which makes the configuration less clean.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and mature, with continuing results on thermalisation and magnetism, though the quantitative impact on solid-state problems is still limited.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with other Bloch and Zoller candidacies on the longlist.
Whether quantum simulation has yet delivered a decisive new physical insight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and quantum control of macroscopic mechanical oscillators, including coupling to superconducting qubits and phonon-number-resolved states, extend quantum mechanics to massive objects and connect to my own field through the Science 2014 type of qubit-phonon coupling. Interesting and clean experiments.
assessment.attribution: Cleland (first quantum mechanical resonator and qubit coupling), Teufel (sideband cooling in circuits) and Aspelmeyer (cavity optomechanics) are reasonable, though Painter, Schwab, Kippenberg, Harris and others also made decisive contributions, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in several platforms, but it is a younger field, with a diffuse set of milestones rather than a single decisive discovery.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse among many groups.
Possibly premature relative to the more established candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and Molenkamp's observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a major new class of matter and a deep link between topology and band structure. Outside my own area, so I defer partly to condensed matter colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele for theory and Molenkamp for the experimental realisation is a sound trio, though Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction, Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan's 3D work are omitted, giving a real credit dispute.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in multiple materials after more than fifteen years. Recognition is timely or perhaps overdue, with a Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz precedent in 2016.
uncertainties: The Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes contribution and 3D topological insulators complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-matter quantum interfaces and atomic quantum memories, from entanglement of atomic ensembles with light to quantum-network nodes, are the basis of long-distance quantum communication. Original and important, and relevant to hybrid quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Polzik, Kimble and Lukin are leading figures, but the field includes Duan, Cirac, Zoller, Lukin, Kuzmich and others in the DLCZ protocol, so credit is unsettled. Lukin also appears in several other entries.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are confirmed, but practical networks remain at an early stage and the discovery is a family of results rather than a single decisive one.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across theory and experiment.
Possibly premature as a prize for the network concept.
